text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- The Turkish army bombed five separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) camps in a cross-border operation into nothern Iraq. A military operation has begun on land with the support of 10,000 village guards.
- The mayor of Istanbul Tayyip Erdogan is working on plans to be the next leader of the Islamist Welfare Party.
MILLIYET
- The state minister responsible for the economy says the government will try to keep 1997 inflation under 100 percent.
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz fiercely defends an eight-year state education plan at a meeting of his party.
HURRIYET
- The two major cola companies, Pepsi Cola and Coca Cola, are investing in the western town of Corlu.
YENI YUZYIL
- Ankara's state security court gave an order to search the Islamist Youth Foundation's headquarters and its branches.
- The chairman of the Istanbul stock exchange dies.
CUMHURIYET
- The prosecutor seeking the closure of the Islamist Welfare Party says closing the party down would be an honourable deed for the constitutional court.
RADIKAL
- The Islamist Welfare Party will seek legal action to block a secularist education bill if it passes through parliament.
DUNYA
- Glass producers Sise Cam and a German group will invest 100 million German marks in a glass producing factory in Istanbul.
ZAMAN
- Dogu Holding's activities in the underdeveloped southeast are faced with "terrorist" threats.
